title: Arterial blood gases: adult normal values and reading a result
applies: Adult values, as the source's own table is titled. A laboratory sets its own reference ranges and critical values, and your hospital's may differ.

capture.of: The rendered text of the chapter as Chrome displayed it on the owner's Mac. Not the page's HTML, images or videos.

licenceCapture.of: The page's licence line, as displayed.

written: Each card is a short statement in Department Hub's own words. Under it are the passages of the captured page it rests on, shown exactly as captured. Every number a card states must appear in those passages, or the cards are refused.

cards.title: Normal arterial blood gas values
cards.where: Table 15.5a, the Adult Normal Value column
cards.answer: Adult normal arterial blood gas values: pH 7.35-7.45, PaO2 80-100 mmHg, PaCO2 35-45 mmHg, HCO3 22-26 mEq/L, SaO2 95-100%.

cards.title: Arterial pH
cards.answer: Adult normal arterial pH is 7.35-7.45. The source lists a pH less than 7.25 or greater than 7.60 as critical, crediting its critical values to one laboratory's 2016 list.

cards.title: PaO2
cards.answer: Adult normal PaO2 is 80-100 mmHg. The source lists a PaO2 less than 60 mmHg as critical, crediting its critical values to one laboratory's 2016 list.

cards.title: PaCO2
cards.answer: Adult normal PaCO2 is 35-45 mmHg. The source lists a PaCO2 less than 25 mmHg or greater than 60 mmHg as critical, crediting its critical values to one laboratory's 2016 list.

cards.title: HCO3 (bicarbonate)
cards.answer: Adult normal HCO3 is 22-26 mEq/L. The source lists an HCO3 less than 10 mEq/L or greater than 40 mEq/L as critical, crediting its critical values to one laboratory's 2016 list.

cards.title: SaO2 (arterial oxygen saturation)
cards.answer: Adult normal SaO2 is 95-100%. The source lists an SaO2 less than 88% as critical, crediting its critical values to one laboratory's 2016 list.

cards.title: Critical arterial blood gas values
cards.where: Table 15.5a, the Critical Value column, and its note [2]
cards.answer: Critical values in the source's adult table: pH less than 7.25 or greater than 7.60; PaO2 less than 60 mmHg; PaCO2 less than 25 mmHg or greater than 60 mmHg; HCO3 less than 10 mEq/L or greater than 40 mEq/L; SaO2 less than 88%. The table credits them to WakeMed Pathology Laboratories' critical values list of 2016.

cards.title: Acidosis or alkalosis, from the pH
cards.answer: A pH less than 7.35 is acidosis. A pH greater than 7.45 is alkalosis.

cards.title: Respiratory acidosis and respiratory alkalosis
cards.answer: The source calls it respiratory acidosis when the pH is less than 7.35 and the PaCO2 is greater than 45, and respiratory alkalosis when the pH is greater than 7.45 and the PaCO2 is less than 35.

cards.title: Metabolic acidosis and metabolic alkalosis
cards.answer: The source calls it metabolic acidosis when the pH is less than 7.35 and the HCO3 is less than 22, and metabolic alkalosis when the pH is greater than 7.45 and the HCO3 is greater than 26.

cards.title: Fully compensated, partially compensated, uncompensated
cards.answer: In the source's step 4: fully compensated means the pH is back to normal (7.35-7.45) while PaCO2 and HCO3 are both out of range. Partially compensated means the pH is still abnormal and PaCO2 and HCO3 are both abnormal. Uncompensated means the pH is abnormal and only one of PaCO2 or HCO3 is abnormal.

cards.title: Which value the lungs manage and which the kidneys
cards.where: Table 15.5a, the PaCO2 and HCO3 descriptions
cards.answer: The source describes CO2 as an acid managed by the lungs and HCO3 as a base managed by the kidneys. As PaCO2 increases the pH decreases; as HCO3 increases the pH increases.
